report.summary: Chunk 6 of docrefs.py: defines scan() and check_denominator() and verify_fix_counts() with docstring claims; enumerates symbols and checks claims against visible code.
risks: scan | medium | The docstring claims 'Never raises.' but the code may raise exceptions from Path operations or iter_doc_files; the try/except only covers OSError on read_text. | Add a try/except around the entire loop or verify that all operations are covered.

scan | low | The overrides dict is built from _rel_key(k) but the key type in overrides is 'repo-relative doc path'; the mapping may not match if k is not a string. | Ensure that all keys in overrides are strings before calling _rel_key.

verify_fix_counts | medium | The function signature uses 'target: Reference | Mapping[str, Any]' but the body only calls check_denominator and does not use target; the docstring claims it is for callers that never held the before-report, but the function is incomplete. | Either implement the rest of verify_fix or remove the unused parameter.
todos: Review scan() for additional exception safety beyond OSError.
Complete verify_fix_counts() implementation or clarify its status.
Add type guards for overrides keys in scan().

handoff.purpose: Defines scan() and verify helper functions with docstring claims.

symbols.name: scan
symbols.note: Reads files from disk, may modify cache dict (mutable default not used).

claims.text: Measure the whole prose corpus against the tree. Never raises.
claims.why: The claim 'Never raises' cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone; only OSError on read_text is caught, but other exceptions (e.g., from Path operations) are not handled.

claims.text: overrides maps a repo-relative doc path to the text to scan INSTEAD of whatever is on disk, or to None meaning 'this file does not exist in the snapshot being measured'.
claims.why: The code at line 627-628 checks if over[rel] is None and continues; if not None, it uses the override text. If the path is not in over, it reads from disk.

claims.text: The MODULE tree is read from repo_root on both sides. That is deliberate: the denominator compares two prose snapshots against ONE tree, so a difference in resolving is attributable to the prose edit and to nothing else.
claims.why: This claim refers to the tree being read from repo_root, but the code only shows scan() reading doc_files and overrides; the tree reading (presumably in resolve_reference) is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: An override may ADD a document the snapshot on disk no longer has -- the deletion case, which is the one the denominator exists to catch.
claims.why: Lines 624-628 handle overrides that are not in seen: if over[rel] is not None, the document is added to planned with path=None, and later at line 632-633 if text is None it continues (skip), else it scans the override text.
The function returns None if resolving_after >= resolving_before, which indicates no destruction.

claims.text: Extracted so the ordering that makes this module safe is STRUCTURAL rather than a paragraph of prose asking the next caller to be careful. Every path that judges a prose fix goes through here first, because verify_fix_counts calls it on its first line and there is no other way in.
claims.why: The claim about verify_fix_counts calling it on its first line is visible (line 680), but 'every path that judges a prose fix goes through here first' cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: It takes counts, not reports, because the count is all the rule needs and a caller that only has a remembered number (the queue's pick-time measurement, carried on a gate command line) must be able to apply the same rule as one holding both full reports.
claims.why: The function signature takes int resolving_before and int resolving_after, not reports.

claims.text: verify_fix with the before-side reduced to its one load-bearing number, for callers that never held the before-report.
claims.why: The function is incomplete; it only calls check_denominator and returns if destroyed, but does not perform the rest of verify_fix. The claim cannot be verified from this chunk.

observations.what: scan() uses a mutable default argument 'cache: dict = {}' which is shared across calls; this can cause unexpected behavior if the cache is modified.
verify_fix_counts has an unused parameter 'target' which is not referenced in the function body.
The docstring of scan() claims 'Never raises' but the code only catches OSError; other exceptions (e.g., ValueError from relative_to) are not caught.
The overrides dictionary keys are processed with _rel_key(k) but the mapping may not match if the caller provides keys with different formats.
